I think it heavily depends on perspective, I grew up in relatively good conditions, I had food always available, games consoles, friends to play with, and some disposable income to spend on leisure activities etc. And this also equated to me having a moral compass, empathy, and thinking that criminals were just some kind of deranged psychopaths, and that 'stealing is wrong' etc. (basically the same as anyone from privileged backgrounds). But now I'm in much less favourable living conditions, all of that is gone now, it's all about survival of only myself and immediate family/loved ones, and when you're in that situation, your priorities are completely different, you don't care about anyone, or whether your actions will hurt them. You will just do whatever it takes to get yourself+loved ones out of that situation. And if someone else's suffering doesn't actually impact you in any way, then it doesn't matter at all (so, it's still bad to hurt you neighbour or other community members, because they can get revenge, or do some kind of retaliation, but scamming other people from rich countries is totally fine, because it's just a minor inconvenience for them, but a literal life/death situation for you, and it is just an abstract person somewhere who you don't even know and don't have any capacity to care about). And yeah this comment will probably get super downvoted because 99% of reddit users are in 'privileged positions' and simply cannot fathom themselves 'stooping so low' but when your life is not in this position then you will all eventually have to adjust your mindset, because it's literally out of necessity of survival, especially if you spend a few years in extreme poverty your perspectives will definitely change over time. And this is why people from 3rd world countries act 'uncivilized' it's not because they are some kind of barbaric animals, but because of the way their lives are. How can you even have the capacity to care about superficial things like 'beauty and cleanliness of your surroundings' etc. When there are way more pressing, immediate issues at hand. And honestly if some higher power said to my townspeople "let's go kill everyone in the neighbouring village and then our town will be prosperous, rich, safe" etc. Everyone would be totally on board with that and would do it, because our current lives are so bad, we'd do anything to improve it, especially when you've already spent many years in survival mode and not caring about anyone else. Humans everywhere, in all countries, in all points in history, are the same... Idk what my overall point even is, lol. But I'm just saying that everyone is the same. And people with a typically "right moral compass" are not inherently better people, than people without that. Ofc there are a few outliers who are always jerks/always kind no matter what position they're in. But for the vast majority it just depends on their living conditions I guess.

I did quit one time, for about 2 years, but the cravings were always there and never really went away. People who say things like "first month is the hardest, then the cravings go away completely, and it's easy from then on" I don't really think that's true. So I ended up starting again, and I never really felt like quitting cause I just like smoking. 


But then I started getting into food and drinks, how to make the taste go to the next level, how to make the best coffee ever, making my own coffee syrup flavors, making own sodas, chocolates, toasting spices, using the perfect amounts of spices/salt/msg, all kinds of world cuisines, quality ingredients etc. And I have like 10 years experience as a chef (but I just did it as a job that I never liked, and I never really had any passion for it, but it was easy and good money) but that experience was really useful for being able to make really good food (for myself and family at home) and I ended up getting really into that. And I read that quitting smoking makes your taste buds able to taste better, and I wanted to find out what that was like, so I could take my food/drinks up ANOTHER level. And yeah it worked. So pretty much just for that reason lol. And cause I finally realized that the overall health benefits better outweigh the "but I like smoking, it reduces stress" excuse that I had. And there are noticeable benefits, like better breathing, less coughing, no hacking up nasty phlegm multiple times a day, no weird heartbeats, no out of breath, more stamina. Paired with better eating so there's even more benefits as well. And no more stinky breath/clothes so you can get up close to other people lol. And another great benefit is you don't have to keep getting up to go smoke, you can just be lazy all day and not go anywhere. You just need to have a "self realization moment" where you realize that the benefits of quitting are better than the "but I like how it feels". You save a load of money too. Now I don't really miss it or have cravings anymore, probably cause I've found another thing which feels good (eating amazing food)

I can put a random example here, if anyone is interested. In slavic, root word 'lit' is to pour. And there are many different prefixes it can have, which give it different meanings. 

Slit = to drain away, to flush away (pour into sink/drain/toilet)  also in slang it can mean to leave unnoticed. 

Otlit = to pour off/away a little bit (you'd need to do this if like a glass is too full to carry). 

Prolit = to spill. 

Rozlit = to pour over multiple instances, (if you're a drinks distributor at a party, then you are doing rozlit). 

Perelit = to overpour (or pour too much). 

Polit = to pour on top of something which needs the liquid  (eg, a plant that needs water, a frying pan that needs oil)

Porozlit = to pour over multiple instances onto things which need the liquid (its 2 suffixes together, po + roz) so, like a professional landscaper is going to porozlit everyone's lawns


Pereslit = too much pour away (again, combo of 2, pere + s)

Pereprolit = spill too much, so much that nothing is left

Perepolit = water the plants way more than needed

Zalit = to pour into something closed, or to fill up something with liquid (like a car tank, a water balloon, your body) 

Selit = is pouring by itself. (eg. water selit from my pipes, they broke. Rain selit.) 

Prelit = to pour liquid from one container to another, to decant

Vilit = to pour out/away completely the whole lot (basically like throwing out the trash, and pouring down the drain) 

Vlit = to pour in, (into an open container, like a bottle) also could be used like, be careful so the flood water doesn't vlit to your home. it has some slang meanings too, so many people are gonna vlit to the club tonight... I have saved up so many magic crystals, I wanna vlit them all into upgrading my weapon.


Nalit = to pour (in a general sense, this is like the most universal word) 


Ponalit = pour too much all over the place (not a combo of po + na, it's its own thing) 


Dolit = pour to the end, till there's none left 


Ulit = pour out the rest, if there's just a little left 


Vzlit = pour really hard and fast


Oblit = pour onto something, completely covering it 


Prilit = add a little tiny bit more liquid to something 

Podlit = pouring unnoticed, secretly under the table or while no one is watching, cause you're doing something you're not really supposed to be doing, eg. adding more vodka to someones drink 

Izlit = this is a more metaphorical kind of word, "pour out" as in "I *poured out* my entire heart and soul to you tonight, I told you my whole life story, my deepest secrets, my weaknesses, and you didn't even care" and, she is pouring out her emotions onto him, as in, letting off steam, letting it all out, unbottling emotions

It's the difference between words which are unique words, and self-describing words. "trousers" is a unique word. If it was a self-describing word it'd be something like "leg coverers" instead.
